stemMd: A town bans heavy vehicles on one street. Counts on that street fall, and officials declare that heavy-vehicle traffic throughout the town has fallen by the same amount. What is the principal flaw?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It assumes the street has no residents.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It treats a town-wide total as an individual driver’s behaviour.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It denies the measured fall on the restricted street.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It ignores the possibility that vehicles shifted to other town streets.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It assumes the banned vehicles are lighter than other vehicles.

explanationMd: The local reduction may be displacement within the town rather than a reduction in the town-wide total. The spatial scope changes between premise and conclusion.

distractorRationale.e: Vehicle weight comparisons are not the inference at issue.
distractorRationale.b: The unsupported move is from one street to the whole town.
distractorRationale.a: Resident count is irrelevant to the stated inference.
